alex: quick Q — I have a user report with request_id=6f8a9c2b. Tried the console logs search but got no hits. Where do we normally look for request_id correlations?

priya: are you using the right key? we log it as `x-rw-req-id` header. console saved search defaults to `trace_id:` so you need to search `request_id:6f8a9c2b` in Logs -> Search. here's a quick URL (open in office network): https://console.redwood.ai/logs?query=request_id%3A6f8a9c2b

matt: cli option if you prefer terminal: `rwctl logs --request-id 6f8a9c2b --service frontend --since 2h` will stream matching lines. example:```bash
# tail server logs and filter
rwctl logs --service frontend --since 1h | rg 6f8a9c2b
```

alex: thanks — when I search in console with `request_id:` I still see nothing. any chance it's sampled out?

priya: possible. we sample traces aggressively for high-traffic endpoints but we should keep request_id logs for all requests. check that you pasted the full id (we sometimes surface a truncated 8-char in UI). also check the response header the client got — we log the exact value.

alex: client header shows `x-rw-req-id: 6f8a9c2b-0a9d`. should I try the full string?

matt: yeah try full string. CLI will match substrings but console search is strict unless you use wildcard. `request_id:6f8a9c2b*` in the console helps.

priya: if you get a trace id instead you can map trace -> request via the traces viewer. e.g. open https://console.redwood.ai/traces and paste the trace id, or `rwctl trace get <trace_id>` to see attributes (look for `http.request.header.x-rw-req-id`).

ops-bot: FYI — saved log query "request_id quick lookup" exists in eng-ml workspace: https://console.redwood.ai/saved-queries/request-id-lookup :eyes:

alex: ah i used the truncated id earlier. searching `request_id:6f8a9c2b-0a9d` returned the lines. thanks! any tips for next time to avoid hunting?

sara: quick checklist we use on support handoffs: 1) capture full `x-rw-req-id` from client; 2) check console saved query (link above); 3) if console empty, try `rwctl logs --request-id` (no sampling there); 4) if you only have trace id, `rwctl trace get` to map back. also note: archived logs older than 30d are in S3 — use `rwctl logs --archive` or ping ops if you need retrieval.

alex: super helpful, closing this one. :thumbsup:
